issues.issue: Does subsection 25(1) of the IRPA, as amended by Bill C-43, bar an H&C application by a person already found inadmissible under section 37?
issues.applicant_position: Is inadmissible in s.25(1) does not bar H&C review of a prior s.37 finding; the bar should be read narrowly.
issues.respondent_position: Section 25(1) is an absolute bar; a prior s.37 inadmissibility finding precludes H&C consideration and cannot be revisited.
issues.result_quote: There is no authority in that legislation which allows an officer to exempt foreign nationals from the requirements of the IRPA on H&C considerations

issues.issue: Can the prior inadmissibility finding be revisited under issue estoppel, given the change in the law from B010?
issues.applicant_position: Issue estoppel's interests-of-justice exception allows revisiting the finding after the B010 change in the law.
issues.respondent_position: Issue estoppel does not apply; H&C officers have no authority to re-determine an ID inadmissibility finding.
issues.result_quote: the doctrine of issue estoppel (or res judicata) has been displaced by the clear language of subsection 25(1) of the IRPA

issues.issue: Does the bar apply to applicants in Canada, or does the Minister keep residual discretion for in-Canada applications?
issues.applicant_position: The bar only removes the mandatory duty for in-Canada applicants, leaving residual discretion to consider the application.
issues.respondent_position: The bar applies equally inside and outside Canada; no residual discretion remains for in-Canada applicants.
issues.result_quote: the amendment was not intended to give the Minister any discretion to process in-Canada applications any differently from those made outside of Canada
